rules.sentence: Screen patients taking anticonvulsants, immunosuppressants, or calcium channel blockers for early signs of drug-induced gingival overgrowth to prevent progression.
Implement appropriate diagnostic protocols, including medical history reviews, drug interaction assessments, and oral examinations, to confirm drug-induced gingival overgrowth.
A non-surgical approach is the first line of treatment, including appropriate plaque control and discontinuing or changing the inducing drug.
In recent years, azithromycin has gained much attention due to its ability to improve gingival overgrowths in patients taking cyclosporin A, avoiding the need to change the drug to another agent.
Surgical management comes into play only when medical treatment is unsuccessful.
However, recurrences are common, and the results usually last 12 months.
